subject: Post-incident readout + evidence transfer for Pelago auth spike
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah@pelago.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pelago Security <security@pelago.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unusual auth spike this morning — request for IRP and logs

Hi Naomi,

We observed an elevated authentication spike affecting a subset of Pelago API keys between 02:00–02:25 UTC this morning (roughly 400% above baseline). No customer data appears exfiltrated, but our SOC team is asking for Redwood's incident response timeline and relevant telemetry exports (auth events, token issuance/validation logs) to complete our audit.

Can you:
- Confirm whether this triggered any Redwood-side alerts or mitigation actions
- Share a sanitized timeline and any available logs (we only need auth-related events and request/response timestamps)
- Provide the incident response plan you would apply for this type of event (SOC 2 / SIG relevant)

We have a 48-hour internal window to capture evidence for our regulator; any help is appreciated.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Security Operations Lead
Pelago Finance

Attachments: none
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah@pelago.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual auth spike this morning — request for IRP and logs

Marissa / Jonas / Ben — looped in you to action Pelago's ask. Sarah, looping you into our internal thread so we keep a single record.

Short plan:
1) Marissa, please collect auth telemetry exports (token issuance, validation, failure codes) from 01:45–02:45 UTC and package as CSV. Mark any PII fields for redaction.
2) Jonas, produce a one-page Redwood timeline of detection/mitigation actions, and include the detection source (alert rule id) + any automatic routing/fallbacks triggered.
3) Ben, prepare our IRP summary (one-page) describing containment, escalation path, and post-incident review cadence — keep it SIG/SOC2 friendly.

We should aim to deliver a first-pass package to Pelago in ~4 hours so they can meet their regulator window. If we need a temporary access window for deeper exports we can set up a scoped S3 share (read-only) and timebox to 72 hours.

Sarah — is redaction guidance (which fields to hide) required from your side? If you can confirm PII masking policy, Marissa will apply it.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

All — attaching the export and my preliminary notes. Deliverables attached:
- pelago_incident_log_export.csv (auth events 2027-04-10 01:45–02:45 UTC, fields: timestamp, client_id, event_type, status_code, src_ip)
- redwood_ir_timeline.pdf (detection -> triage -> mitigation timeline, includes alert ids)
- pelago_postmortem_notes.docx (internal notes; redaction placeholders left for customer review)

Key observations (quick):
- Spike origin correlated with a burst of requests from three client_ids; two of those client_ids are active Pelago subkeys.
- Auth failures rose sharply at 02:03 UTC and returned to baseline by 02:22 UTC after rate-limiting rule triggered at 02:05 UTC.
- No token creation anomalies (no unauthorized token issuance observed).

Action items for Pelago to confirm:
- Confirm which fields you require redacted in the CSV (full IPs vs /24 masking; client_id masking)
- If you need deeper traces (request payloads), we will need explicit approval and a scoped access window; otherwise the CSV above should satisfy SOC 2 evidence requirements for auth events.

I applied default redaction to account_email fields in the draft CSV. Let me know if you want raw values for forensics (we can provision ephemeral access).

Marissa Cole
Security Operations Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pelago_incident_log_export.csv, redwood_ir_timeline.pdf, pelago_postmortem_notes.docx

Hi Sarah / Tom — thank you for the quick heads-up and patience. Attached is the package we've prepared for your audit window. Summary below, and attachments are the three files Marissa generated.

Executive summary (short):
- Event: Increased authentication attempts affecting Pelago-managed API keys detected 2027-04-10 02:00–02:25 UTC.
- Immediate action: Redwood's rate-limiting rule 27-auth-threshold triggered at 02:05 UTC, reducing request throughput. No automatic key rotation occurred.
- Outcome: Request rate returned to baseline at ~02:22 UTC. No evidence of data exfiltration or anomalous token issuance.

What we are delivering now:
- pelago_incident_log_export.csv (auth events with minimal PII; we masked client IPs to /24 by default)
- redwood_ir_timeline.pdf (detection and mitigation timeline with alert IDs)
- pelago_postmortem_notes.docx (internal notes with redaction placeholders)

Next steps and options:
- If Pelago requires unredacted IPs or payload traces for your forensic review, reply with the minimal justification and scope; we'll provision a time-limited S3 bucket (read-only) and log access for compliance.
- We propose a joint post-incident readout call tomorrow (2027-04-11) at 14:00 UTC to walk through the timeline and any follow-up telemetry requests. Please confirm availability.

Regulatory note: We maintain the evidence package for 90 days in a scoped evidence bucket; if you need an extended retention window for regulator review, we can extend per written request.

Thanks again — happy to jump on a call.

Naomi Feldman
